items.title: Seven Ways a Future Thing Might "Arrive" at the Present — All Refuted

items.zh: 又今問汝，隨汝意答。為計未來法來至現在世耶？為彼死已，於此生耶？為即住未來為緣，生現在耶？為本無業，今有業耶？為本相不圓滿，今相圓滿耶？為本異相，今異相耶？為於未來有現在分耶？
items.en: Further, I now ask you, answer as you see fit: do you hold that a future phenomenon arrives in the present world? Or that it dies, and only then is born here? Or that, remaining in the future, it serves as a condition that gives rise to the present? Or that it has no function while future, and gains a function now? Or that its characteristic is incomplete while future, and becomes complete now? Or that its characteristic while future differs from its characteristic now? Or that a portion of the present already exists within the future?

items.zh: 若即未來法來至現在者，此便有方所；復與現在應無差別；復應是常；不應道理。若言未來死已現在生者，是即未來不生於今；現在世法本無今生；又未來未生而言死沒；不應道理。
items.en: If a future phenomenon simply arrives in the present, it would have to already occupy a location — it would then be indistinguishable from a present phenomenon, and would have to be permanent; none of this makes sense. If you say it dies while future and is then born in the present, then what was future does not itself give rise to the present; the present phenomenon would then have no genuine "arising" at all; and, further, to speak of something dying that was never even born makes no sense.

items.zh: 若言法住未來，以彼為緣生現在者，彼應是常；又應本無今生，非未來法生；不應道理。若本無業用，今有業用，是則本無今有，便有如前所說過失，不應道理。
items.en: If you say the phenomenon, remaining in the future, serves as a condition producing the present, then it would have to be permanent, and, again, the present would have no genuine arising and would not actually be produced by the future; this makes no sense. If it has no function while future and only gains a function now, this is again a case of something nonexistent becoming existent, carrying the same faults already stated; this makes no sense.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？此業用與彼本法為有異相？為無異相？若有異相，此業用相未來無故，不應道理。若無異相，本無業用，今有業用，不應道理。
如無業用有此過失，如是相圓滿、異相、未來分相應知亦爾。此中差別者，復有自性雜亂過失故，不應道理。如未來向現在如是，現在往過去，如其所應過失應知。
items.en: Just as the "gaining a function" claim carries this fault, so too should the "characteristic becomes complete," "characteristic differs," and "a portion already present" claims each be understood to carry it as well. What further distinguishes these is the fault of the very self-nature of the phenomenon becoming confused — one and the same thing being, at once, incomplete and complete, or both cause-aspect and result-aspect; this makes no sense. Just as these faults apply to the future becoming present, so too, correspondingly, should they be understood to apply to the present passing into the past.

items.zh: 謂即如前所計諸因緣及所說破道理。

items.title: If Past and Future Aren't Real, How Can the Mind Even Think About Them?

items.zh: 如是自相故，共相故，來故，死故，為緣生故，業故，相圓滿故，相異故，未來有分故，說過去未來體實有論，不應道理。
items.en: Thus, through self-characteristic, through shared characteristic, through arrival, through dying, through serving as a condition of production, through function, through completeness of characteristic, through difference of characteristic, and through the future already containing a portion of the present — through these nine approaches, the doctrine that the substance of past and future truly exists does not accord with reason.

items.zh: 復有難言：若過去、未來是無，云何緣無而有覺轉？若言緣無而有覺轉者，云何不有違教過失？如說：一切有者，謂十二處。我今問汝，隨汝意答。世間取無之覺為起耶？為不起耶？若不起者，能取無我、兔角、石女兒等覺皆應是無，此不應理。又薄伽梵說：我諸無諂聲聞，如我所說正修行時，若有知有，若無知無。此不應道理。若言起者，汝意云何？此取無覺，為作有行？為作無行？若作有行，取無之覺而作有行，不應道理。若作無行者，汝何所欲？此無行覺，為緣有事轉？為緣無事轉？若緣有事轉者，無行之覺緣有事轉，不應道理。若緣無事轉者，無緣無覺，不應道理。
items.en: A further objection is raised: if the past and future do not exist, how can cognition operate by taking something nonexistent as its object? And if cognition can indeed operate by taking something nonexistent as its object, how does this not contradict the Buddha's own teaching that "all that exists" is the twelve sense-bases? I now ask you in turn, answer as you see fit: does the world's cognition of what is nonexistent arise at all, or does it not? If it does not arise, then cognition taking non-self, a hare's horn, or a barren woman's child as its object should likewise be nonexistent — which makes no sense.

items.title: The Hidden Intent Behind "All That Exists Is the Twelve Sense-Bases"

items.zh: 又雖說一切有者，謂十二處；然於有法密意說有有相，於無法密意說有無相。所以者何？若有相法能持有相，若無相法能持無相；是故俱名為法，俱名為有。若異此者，諸修行者唯知於有，不知於無；應非無間觀所知法，不應道理。
items.en: Further, although it is said that "all that exists" refers to the twelve sense-bases, this is spoken with hidden intent: of what has existent characteristics, it is said to have the characteristic of existing; of what has no such characteristics, it is said to have the characteristic of not existing. Why is this? Because whatever has an existent characteristic can sustain that existent characteristic, and whatever has no such characteristic can sustain that absence — and so both alike are called a "phenomenon," and both alike are called "existent." Were it otherwise, practitioners would know only the existent and never the nonexistent, and so could not contemplate every knowable phenomenon comprehensively, without omission — which makes no sense.

items.title: "Past Karma Exists" Really Means Its Habitual Imprint Persists

items.zh: 又雖說言有過去業；由此業故，諸有情受有損害受、無損害受。此亦依彼習氣，密意假說為有。謂於諸行中，曾有淨不淨業若生若滅。由此因緣，彼行勝異相續而轉，是名習氣。由此相續所攝習氣故，愛不愛果生。是故於我無過，而汝不應道理。
items.en: Further, although it is said that past karma exists, and that by reason of this karma beings experience harmful or harmless feeling, this too is spoken provisionally, with hidden intent, in reference to its habitual imprint. That is: among the formations, pure or impure karma once arose and ceased. By reason of this, those formations continue on, transformed and intensified in succession — this is called a habitual imprint. It is by reason of this habitual imprint, held within the mental continuum, that desirable and undesirable results arise. There is, therefore, no fault in my position — it is your own position that does not accord with reason.

items.title: Cause-Aspect, Own-Aspect, Result-Aspect: Why Form Is Called Past, Present, and Future

items.zh: 復雖說言有過去色、有未來色、有現在色，如是乃至識亦爾者，此亦依三種行相密意故說。謂因相、自相、果相。依彼因相，密意說有未來；依彼自相，密意說有現在；依彼果相，密意說有過去，是故無過。
items.en: Further, although it is said that past form exists, future form exists, and present form exists, and so on in the same way through consciousness, this too is spoken with hidden intent, in reference to three aspects: the cause-aspect, the own-aspect, and the result-aspect. It is with reference to the cause-aspect that future existence is spoken of with hidden intent; with reference to the own-aspect that present existence is spoken of with hidden intent; and with reference to the result-aspect that past existence is spoken of with hidden intent. There is, therefore, no fault in this teaching.

items.zh: 又不應說過去、未來是實有相。何以故？

blocks.text: Today the treatise finishes refuting the real existence of past and future, and then, more importantly, explains what the Buddha meant when he spoke as if they existed. The key idea, **hidden intent** (密意), is one Yogācāra uses constantly: a teaching may be true in what it intends while misleading if read literally.
Untranslated: 0304c29–0305a03 (a further dilemma about whether a thing's function differs from its nature), 0305a07, 0305a10, and 0305b11 (short connecting phrases).

If future things exist and come into the present, how do they come? The treatise tests seven possibilities. Master Cháng Bǎi on the first, that the future thing must then occupy a location: "The future hasn't come yet; how can you know whether it's east, west, south, or north? Like tomorrow: where is it?" Venerable Miào Jìng adds, candidly, "If we don't study, I think this 'three times truly exist' is very hard to refute." It feels natural to imagine time as a road along which things travel.
The treatise sums up nine approaches by which the doctrine fails.

subs.head: Thinking of what does not exist

blocks.text: The opponent's strongest argument: cognition must have an object, so if we can think of the past, the past must exist. The treatise answers that cognition takes the nonexistent as object all the time. Master Cháng Bǎi: people think about non-self, a hare's horn, a barren woman's child. Venerable Miào Jìng: "you may dream of a man with horns." A thought having content does not make the content exist.
This is a significant step towards consciousness-only. What appears to cognition need not exist outside it.

subs.head: "All that exists is the twelve sense-bases"

blocks.text: The Buddha did say that. But it was spoken with **hidden intent**. Venerable Miào Jìng explains the idea with a Chinese saying: "The old drunkard's mind is not on the wine but on the hills and waters"; the surface meaning is not the main one. The Buddha meant: of what exists, the twelve sense-bases are what exists; he was not saying that past and future things exist.

The Buddha said past karma exists. This too is said provisionally, with reference to its **habitual imprint** (習氣): after a deed arises and ceases, the stream of formations continues, changed, and "it is by reason of this habitual imprint, held within the mental continuum, that desirable and undesirable results arise."

Here is the answer to Day 39's worry. Karma does not need a real past deed sitting somewhere in time. It needs only a present seed. The seed theory of Day 1 does the work that the Sarvāstivāda tried to do with real past and future.

And past and future form? Again hidden intent. Form is called future with reference to its **cause-aspect** (the seed not yet ripened), present with reference to its **own-aspect** (what is arising now), and past with reference to its **result-aspect** (the imprint it leaves). All three are aspects of what is present. Time, as Day 18 said, has no substance of its own.
This is a fine example of how Yogācāra reads scripture: not rejecting the Buddha's words but locating what they refer to.

quiz.q: The second dilemma asks whether things in the three times are permanent or impermanent. What fault does each answer bring?
options: if permanent, falling into three times makes no sense; if impermanent, being perpetually real through the three times makes no sense
quiz.why: "If permanent, then for it to fall within three distinct times at all makes no sense. If impermanent, then for it to be equally, perpetually, truly existent throughout all three times makes no sense." Master Cháng Bǎi: "What is permanent doesn't change; to speak of three times without change makes no sense." Venerable Miào Jìng insists in a Q&A: "Truly existent means permanent."

quiz.q: "If a future phenomenon simply arrives in the present, it would have to occupy a location." How does Master Cháng Bǎi illustrate this fault?
options: the future hasn't come — how can it be east, west, north, or south? like asking where tomorrow is before it comes
a bird returning to its nest
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The future dharma hasn't come yet — how can you know whether it's east, west, south, or north? Like tomorrow: it hasn't come, so where is it?" The text adds that it would then be indistinguishable from the present and permanent. Venerable Miào Jìng recounts a student objecting that this uses space to refute time; he answers that if it exists, it has a place — so where?

quiz.q: Through which nine approaches does the text conclude that the substantial existence of past and future does not hold?
options: self-characteristic, shared characteristic, arrival, dying, serving as a condition, function, completeness, difference of characteristic, and the future containing a portion of the present
quiz.why: "Thus, through self-characteristic, through shared characteristic, through arrival, through dying, through serving as a condition of production, through function, through completeness of characteristic, through difference of characteristic, and through the future already containing a portion of the present." The first two are §11's dilemmas, the last seven §12's questions. Venerable Miào Jìng: "Nine 'because' — a summary."

quiz.q: The opponent asks how cognition can take the nonexistent as object. The text counters with ordinary cognitions of the nonexistent. What examples do the teachers give?
options: people can think about non-self, a hare's horn, a barren woman's child; one may dream of a man with horns
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "In fact people can think about and discriminate non-self, a hare's horn, a barren woman's child." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Say you dream of a man with horns — people have no horns, so how?" Since cognition of the nonexistent does arise, cognizing past and future needn't make them real. He adds that the five sense-consciousnesses take only the present; only the sixth can take past and future.

quiz.q: The text says "all that exists is the twelve sense-bases" was spoken with hidden intent. What saying does Venerable Miào Jìng use to explain "hidden intent"?
options: "The old drunkard's mind is not on the wine but on the hills and waters" — the surface meaning isn't the main one
"Among three walking, one is my teacher"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The surface meaning isn't the main one; it points elsewhere — 'the old drunkard's mind is not on the wine but on the hills and waters.'" The text: of what exists, it means it has existent marks; of what doesn't, it means it has the mark of not existing. "Dharma" means "to hold": both hold their marks, so both are called dharmas and "existent."

quiz.q: The Buddha said past karma exists. According to the treatise, this is said provisionally with reference to what?
options: its habitual imprint — after pure or impure karma arises and ceases, the formations continue, transformed; from this imprint held in the continuum, desirable and undesirable results arise
quiz.why: "This too is spoken provisionally, with hidden intent, in reference to its habitual imprint … It is by reason of this habitual imprint, held within the mental continuum, that desirable and undesirable results arise." Master Cháng Bǎi: "'Past karma exists' means the seed it perfumed, not that the past deed is still real." Venerable Miào Jìng: it doesn't stay in the past but keeps becoming the present.

quiz.q: The Buddha spoke of past, future, and present form. According to the treatise, through which three aspects, and how do they map to the three times?
options: cause-aspect → future, own-aspect → present, result-aspect → past
quiz.why: "It is with reference to the cause-aspect that future existence is spoken of with hidden intent; with reference to the own-aspect that present existence …; and with reference to the result-aspect that past existence." Master Cháng Bǎi: keeping the five precepts now is the cause of a future human birth — said to show impermanence. Venerable Miào Jìng: "The past is still nonexistent, the future too; only the present exists." C reverses it.
